risks.risk: Revenue concentration in domestic mutual fund investor solutions
risks.note: This segment accounts for a dominant share of revenue and is sensitive to AUM-linked fees, asset mix shifts, and mark-to-market gains, making profitability vulnerable to equity market volatility and FPI outflows.

risks.risk: Integration and performance risk from Ascent acquisition
risks.note: The transformational acquisition of Ascent Fund Services adds scale and geographic diversification but introduces execution risk in integrating operations, retaining talent, and achieving targeted international revenue contribution of 25â30% over 4â5 years.

risks.risk: Margin pressure from evolving asset mix and lower MTM gains
risks.note: A shift in investor allocation towards passive and precious metal-linked products, combined with softer mark-to-market gains, compresses AUM-linked fee yields and overall EBITDA margins, particularly in the core domestic mutual fund business.

risks.risk: Competitive talent market and rising employee costs
risks.note: High replacement costs, targeted hiring for specialized domain expertise, and annual increments in a competitive talent market drive employee benefit expenses, which rose 30.20% YoY, challenging cost discipline.

risks.risk: Regulatory and compliance risk in multi-jurisdictional operations
risks.note: As the company scales globally through subsidiaries across South-East Asia, GIFT City, and other markets, it faces evolving regulatory frameworks, data privacy requirements, and compliance complexity, with any failure potentially leading to reputational damage or operational restrictions.

Strategic investments in cloud, cybersecurity, and data centre capabilities are essential to support scalable platforms, but any breach, system failure, or inadequate data governance could disrupt operations, erode client trust, and lead to financial loss.

risks.risk: Moderation in primary issuances and corporate action volumes
risks.note: Issuer Solutions revenue growth is tied to capital market activity; a sustained slowdown in primary issuances or corporate actions due to market volatility can suppress folio additions and fee income, impacting segment performance.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Structural financialisation of Indian household savings, formalisation of the economy, and rising SIP flows (crossing ~₹3.5 trillion annually) support long-term domestic demand.
- Global asset management AUM growth of 11% YoY to ~US$147 trillion, with retail investors driving over 60% of expansion and Asia-Pacific growing faster, creating demand for scalable platforms.
- Alternatives AUM projected to reach US$29+ trillion by 2029 and US$32 trillion by 2032, with outsourcing of fund administration, middle-office, and data services accelerating as a structural necessity.
- Tokenisation of fund AUM projected to grow from US$90 billion in 2024 to US$715 billion by 2030 (40%+ CAGR), requiring new digital asset servicing and on-chain reporting capabilities.
- AI expected to unlock 25–35% cost efficiencies in asset management, driving demand for AI-native platforms and integrated data-centric solutions.
- Regulatory intensity (AML/KYC, AIFMD II, ESG) and LP demands for real-time, granular reporting are pushing asset managers to outsource to technology-enabled strategic infrastructure partners.
- India's economic growth projected at 6.8–7.2% in FY27, supported by public investment, structural reforms, and resilient domestic demand.

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Transform from an India-centric RTA into a scaled, globally relevant financial infrastructure platform serving institutional investment managers across asset classes, jurisdictions, and currencies.
- Scale emerging growth engines — Fund Administration, Alternatives, Pension Services, Wealth Solutions, and Data Platforms — as structural growth engines diversifying revenue beyond the core business.
- Expand international footprint, leveraging the Ascent Fund Services integration to extend presence across 18+ countries and deploy India-developed technology and operating models globally.
- Embed AI and data capabilities as foundational elements across platforms, moving from transaction processing to insight-driven service delivery via agent-assisted, human-supervised operating models and a governed data lake architecture.
- Deepen client relationships and strengthen governance, cybersecurity, operational resilience, and regulatory compliance as the business scales in complexity and geographic reach.
- The provided annual-report text does not contain a dividend policy, buyback, debt reduction, credit rating, or reinvestment intent statement.
- Achieved zero regulatory warning observations for three consecutive years, demonstrating strong governance and compliance culture.
- Implemented an integrated enterprise-wide risk management (ERM) and data privacy framework with real-time risk tracking, dashboards, and 100% user adoption across 32 functions and subsidiaries.
- Employee turnover rate for permanent employees stood at 25% in FY26, with a focus on building a collaborative, inclusive, and high-engagement culture supported by diversity initiatives.
- Board composition includes 10% women directors, and women represent 33% of Key Management Personnel (KMP).
- CSR is applicable under Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013, with the company undertaking community initiatives as part of its broader responsibility.
- Reasonable assurance obtained from SGS India Pvt Ltd. on core BRSR indicators, covering 73% of total carpet area across 5 office locations.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Mission-critical infrastructure with high throughput and global reach, creating a self-reinforcing scale advantage that lowers marginal costs.
- Deep technology moat through proprietary AI, cloud-native architecture, and automation, embedding into client workflows and creating high switching costs and long-term stickiness.
- Highly predictable, recurring revenue model with 99.8% recurring revenue and 97-98% client retention ratio, supported by 10+ year client relationships in domestic mutual fund business.
- Capital-efficient, cash-generative model with 51.0% EBITDA to free cash flow conversion and 57.2% return on tangible equity.
- Diversified, multi-vector growth engine spanning asset classes, client segments, and geographies, reducing concentration risk.
